en: Looks only. Nothing sold here changes the game.
Drag in the lower screen to walk. Your hands remember the rest: you fire on your own. Destroy both targets.
A turret. Walk next to the crate, then lift your finger: you slide into cover behind it.
Bullets are coming. Flick and release quickly to roll through them. Rolls make you untouchable for a moment. Roll twice.
Too many bullets? Double-tap anywhere to fire your EMP. It wipes every enemy bullet off the screen.
The Warden's archive. One recording, filed under 'trophies'.
Coolant slows you. Firewalls sweep: roll through them.
A broken phone on the belt. It still has one message.
Belts move you. Molten metal burns. Roll across it.
A stall that sells crayons. She would have loved it.
Everything is an ad. Nothing is what it seems.
Walk through a door to begin
A projector in a dead penthouse. It still holds one hologram.
Lasers blink before they burn. Cracked glass gives way.
The Core goes dark. Zero's red eye flickers, and goes out.
The Syndicate's backups burn, one server at a time.
Vorn: One last upgrade, Sergeant. Just to be sure.
Kade: No. I'm done being fixed.
The memorial. He sets Button down beside the photo. The music box plays, clean.
Kade: I'm still here. That's how I know I won.
The Core goes dark. Zero's red eye flickers, and goes out.
Rain on Halcyon. Some memories are simply gone, where the machines went in.
The music box skips a note. He doesn't notice.
He keeps walking. He is not sure where.
The Core goes dark. Zero's red eye flickers, and goes out.
Rain on Halcyon. Half his face catches the neon. Most of what he lost, he can still remember losing.
The music box skips a note. He hums the missing one himself.
Zero's red eye goes out. Another one opens.
The Syndicate's robots kneel to the stronger machine.
MEMORY LOW. One personal file left: lullaby.wav. Delete to free space?
A new Zero, red-eyed, on a throne of servers. You became what you wanted to destroy.
Servo Arms. His hands stopped shaking. He used to like that they shook.
Neural Coprocessor. Thoughts arrive before he finishes having them.
Vorn: If something feels missing, tell me. I keep notes.
Hawk Optics. The world comes with numbers now.
Vorn: Read me the chart on the wall. ...From the next room.
Fusion Heart. It keeps time like a metronome now.
Vorn: Steady as a clock, Sergeant. Steadier than you.
Hydraulic Legs. The floor feels farther away.
Vorn: Walk for me. Slowly. They remember running before you do.
Filter Lungs. The air tastes like nothing now.
Vorn: You can stop holding your breath. You'll never need to again.
Halcyon. A city where the machines keep the peace, and one family keeps a music box.
Mira: Again! Play it again, Dad!
Then the wall came in. Then the lights died.
Kade fought with his bare hands. It wasn't enough.
Nine days later. Somewhere under the city.
Vorn: You're alive. They're not. I'm sorry.
A grieving veteran. A city of machines. Five districts.
Placeholder art, sound and music made for the prototype
tap to return to the lab
Dr. Vorn's drone dragged you out of the scrap. The run is over; your Crypto, RAM and implants are kept.
Watch a short ad to get back up with 1 heart and a free EMP. Once per run.
Every part you replace is a part of the man.
A photo, curled at the corners. Kade and Lena in the rain outside the registry office, soaked to the skin and laughing. She painted the umbrella herself. It leaked.
A photo. Lena in the rain, laughing at something. I was laughing too. I think the umbrella leaked.
A photo of two people in the rain. One of them is me. She's laughing. I know her name. Lena. I know it.
Image file: wedding_01.jpg. Subjects: 2. Weather: rain. Classification: personal. ...Do not delete.
A crayon drawing: the three of them under an enormous yellow sun. "She drew us like this every day. Me always bigger than the house."
A crayon drawing. "Her drawing. I remember the colors. Mostly."
A drawing. Three figures. "I know it mattered. I can't feel why."
Image file: drawing_family.png. Emotional weight: unknown. ...Keep.
A voice message, the last one on his old phone. Lena, laughing, Mira shouting in the background: "Come home safe. We saved you cake."
A voice message. "Come home safe. We saved you..." The rest is noise. He plays it again anyway.
Audio file. A woman's voice. "Come home safe." He knows it was meant for him. He replays it to make sure.
Audio file: msg_0412.ogg. Duration: 0:07. Speaker: Lena. Content: request for safe return. ...Archive.
A hologram, flickering: Mira blowing out seven candles, Button the rabbit propped up beside her plate. She missed one. Kade blew it out for her.
A hologram. Mira and the candles. Seven, he thinks. The rabbit was there. The rabbit was always there.
A hologram of a child and a cake. "Seven candles. I counted them. I don't remember why that mattered."
Hologram file: bday_07.holo. Candles: 7. Toy present: 1 (rabbit, "Button"). Significance: high. ...Do not compress.

The Warden's recording. Mostly sound. The music box. A wall giving way. Lena saying his name, steady. Then a red light, close, and a voice: "Live with it, Sergeant." He listens to the end. He makes himself.
The recording. Sound and shapes. The music box, Lena's voice, the dark. Then: "Live with it, Sergeant." He stops it there.
A recording of the night. He knows what happens in it. He plays it anyway, waiting to feel it. "Live with it, Sergeant."
Recording: night_0.rec. Hostiles: 4. Survivors: 1. Final line, source ZERO: "Live with it, Sergeant." ...Purpose: confirmed.
The Syndicate keeps backups, Sergeant. Kill one and it wakes up angry by morning.
All five lieutenants in one night. Then they stay dead.
Glitch. The one who faked the police call. Nobody came for your family because of that thing.
It came apart like a cheap sign.
Holograms do. The Foundry builds the real bodies. That is where this goes next.
You're adapting faster than any patient I've had. I'm proud of that. Is that strange?
Forgemother called her robots her children. I knew a woman like that, once. A long time ago.
She built the ones who came for my family.
And now she builds nothing. The Spires are next: the Warden watched everything that night.
You came back with fewer scars than I expected. Some of that is you. Some of it is me.
The Warden kept recordings of everything. Including that night.
The Syndicate Core. Zero keeps it close. A trophy. Patch dug up your old service rifle while you were out.
Before you go down there: whatever is on that recording, you are still the one who decides what it makes of you.
Welcome back to the land of the living, Sergeant. Mostly living.
The machines that did this. Where are they?
The Null Syndicate. Their first lieutenant, Scrapjaw, holds the Rustline. The elevator goes there.
When you're ready... I can make you better. The chair is right here.
And when you're done being noble, I sell guns. Meat's honest, and so are my prices.
That gun? Found it in a toaster. Well. It was a toaster.
Stashed in the Rustline. Check the chests, and don't tell Vorn where I hide things.
Pleasure. Meat's honest, and so is my merchandise. Mostly.
Another one? You're my favorite customer. You're also my only customer.
My drone found you in a scrap heap. Lie still. You're home.
Again? My drone is getting good at this.
They come back from backups, Sergeant. You come back from me. Rest.
You keep coming back. That's the part they never understand about you.
Your vitals are perfect. Perfect worries me more than it should.
You stopped asking what each part does. You only ask what it costs.
I wanted to make you better. I keep checking whether I did.
Still all you, Sergeant. I admire it. I also count the days it costs you.
The chair isn't a threat. It's an offer. Offers keep.
You fight like a man with something to lose. Keep it, if you can.
Extraordinary. I never thought I'd see it finished.
Do you still dream, Sergeant? I'd like to know. For the notes.
Whatever happens down there, it was always going to be you.
How does it feel? Don't answer like a soldier. Answer like a patient.
Every part I give you is a part you chose. Remember that when it matters.
You walk differently now. Lighter. Your daughter would have noticed.
Steadier hands than the ones you were born with.
Point. Don't aim. The arm knows.
Dual Wield: both carried guns fire at once.
Two hands, two guns, no hesitation. I built it for exactly one person.
A little more room upstairs. You won't miss what I moved.
EMP stun radius 4 to 6 tiles, and the stun lasts 2.5 s.
Think louder, Sergeant. The machines will hear you.
Failsafe: once per level, a lethal hit fires a free EMP and is negated.
If you die now, it will be because you chose to.
Auto-aim range +25%. Your target's HP is shown.
See them before they see you. That was always the job, wasn't it?
+15% chance of a critical hit (double damage).
Every weak point, lit up like a shop window.
Threat Sight: enemy tells last 0.2 s longer, and bullets aimed at you are highlighted.
Now you see what's coming. Some nights I wish I couldn't.
There. A heart that won't stop. Not for anything, Sergeant.
It hums now. You'll stop hearing the hum. Most do.
+1 more max heart. Heal 1/2 heart every 3 cleared rooms.
Every part I give you is a part you chose.
Faster than any man alive. Technically.
Jump, Sergeant. See how far away the ground is now.
Every roll ends in a shockwave: 10 damage within 1.5 tiles, and it clears bullets.
You were always going to come to me, Sergeant.
Breathe. Or don't. It matters less every day.
Immune to gas, fire and molten floors. Roll i-frames 60% to 75%.
The Foundry can't burn what doesn't need air.
Second Wind: rolling through an enemy bullet slows time for 0.4 s and gives +20% damage for 3 s.
Every close call is a gift, Sergeant. Spend it.
Subject declined every upgrade. Outcome: better than anything I could have made of him. Note to self: stop offering.
He won with what I gave him and lost what I took. Every part was his choice. I made sure it was.
He kept most of himself. I kept my notes. I am still not sure which of us got the better deal.
Project complete. He is everything I built him to be. I should feel proud. I should feel something.
Kade's own. Worn through every district.
Matte black. Bullets stay the same.
It refuses to die. Vorn waters it.
